newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN QUIET TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN QUIET TRADE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed in fairly quiet trade on Tuesday.
Dealers said although the market closed short on Monday, liquidity was expected to improve on Tuesday with a number of treasury bills maturing.
"At the moment the market is still very quiet," one dealer said in the morning.
He said there were no buyers for 30, 60 and 90-day NCDs but discount houses were indicating 18.70 percent from 18.75, and were selling the paper at 18.25 percent from 18.50 percent the previous day.
Bankers acceptances were quoted firmer at 17.90 and 17.65 percent (buying and selling respectively) from Monday's 17.80 and 17.50 percent, while call money held steady at 17.50 percent.
Figures from the central Reserve Bank showed a Z$56 million shortage at Monday's close, from a previous surplus of Z$39 million.
